diagrams.title: Initial Dermatomyositis Evaluation
diagrams.subtitle: A clinic-ready sequence from recognition to organ-risk stratification

items.label: Full skin, scalp, oral, and nailfold examination
items.detail: Document Gottron papules/sign, heliotrope, photodistributed poikiloderma, scalp disease, mechanic’s hands, palmar papules, ulcers/necrosis, calcinosis, and activity versus damage.

items.label: Focused neuromuscular history and examination
items.detail: Ask about stairs, rising from a chair/floor, overhead tasks, falls, neck weakness, myalgia, dysphagia, dysphonia, and aspiration.

items.label: Classic, hypomyopathic, or clinically amyopathic
items.detail: A normal CK or normal bedside strength does not exclude subclinical muscle disease.

items.label: Look for overlap features
items.detail: Raynaud, sclerodactyly, inflammatory arthritis, mechanic’s hands, sicca, or lupus features may change serology interpretation and treatment.

items.label: CK, aldolase, LDH, AST/ALT
items.detail: Interpret trends and baseline variation; AST/ALT can be muscle-derived.

items.label: Myositis-specific/associated antibody panel
items.detail: Use to refine phenotype, cancer risk, and ILD risk; verify unexpected results with clinical context and assay limitations.

items.label: CBC, CMP and treatment-safety tests
items.detail: Add infection screening, pregnancy testing, immunization review, and other tests based on anticipated therapy.

items.label: Weakness plus enzyme elevation
items.detail: In a patient with convincing DM skin findings, this often establishes muscle involvement without muscle biopsy.

items.label: Discordant symptoms, examination, or enzymes
items.detail: Obtain MRI of bilateral thighs with myositis protocol; consider EMG or biopsy when an alternative myopathy remains plausible.

items.label: PFTs; HRCT according to risk and guideline framework
items.detail: Use a low threshold in MDA5, antisynthetase, mechanic’s hands, arthritis, dyspnea, or ulcerative disease.

items.label: IMACS risk-stratified cancer screening
items.detail: Complete age/sex-appropriate screening and add basic/enhanced testing by risk.

items.label: Swallowing, aspiration, cardiac, and functional assessment
items.detail: Escalate dysphagia, aspiration, rapid weakness, or cardiopulmonary symptoms.

items.label: Track each domain separately
items.detail: Skin activity can persist after muscle improvement and vice versa. Repeat muscle review and testing during the early disease course even in initially amyopathic disease.

citations.quote: Garg, Merola, and Fitzpatrick (eds.). Interdisciplinary Approaches to Overlap Disorders in Dermatology & Rheumatology. Springer, 2022.
Concha et al. review diagnostic and classification limitations in amyopathic dermatomyositis, including overlap with lupus.
Myositis-specific autoantibodies define clinically useful dermatomyositis phenotypes, including MDA5, TIF1γ, NXP2, Mi-2, and SAE associations.
IMACS international guideline provides risk-stratified cancer screening recommendations for idiopathic inflammatory myopathies.
ACR/CHEST guideline conditionally recommends PFTs and HRCT for screening people with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases at risk for ILD.

diagrams.title: Dermatomyositis Muscle Assessment
diagrams.subtitle: What to do when strength, symptoms, and enzymes do not line up

steps.detail: If the cutaneous diagnosis is uncertain, biopsy an active lesion and maintain a broad differential; skin histology alone may not distinguish DM from CLE.
Photograph distribution, examine nailfolds and scalp, biopsy if needed, and consider CLE, psoriasis, contact/photoallergic dermatitis, and drug eruption.

steps.prompt: Objective symmetric proximal weakness or major functional decline?
Any muscle enzyme elevated (CK, aldolase, LDH, AST/ALT)?

steps.detail: Stage severity, assess swallowing/respiratory involvement, begin appropriate systemic therapy, and reserve biopsy for atypical or discordant cases.

steps.prompt: Myalgia, soreness, fatigue, subtle functional loss, dysphagia, or high-risk phenotype?
MRI shows muscle/fascial edema compatible with inflammatory myopathy?
Classify as muscle-involved or hypomyopathic DM in context
steps.detail: Use examination, imaging, enzymes, and trajectory together; MRI can also guide a biopsy if needed.
Examples: immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, inclusion-body myositis, muscular dystrophy, metabolic/toxic myopathy, neuropathy, deconditioning, or steroid myopathy.

steps.prompt: Use EMG, targeted muscle biopsy, neurology input, and focused testing
steps.detail: Choose a clinically/MRI-involved but not end-stage muscle; avoid treating an unverified alternative diagnosis as DM.
Recheck strength/function and enzymes; repeat imaging if the phenotype evolves.
Continue periodic strength, symptom, and enzyme review, especially during the first years and whenever new weakness, dysphagia, or respiratory symptoms appear.
